scope: Core OpenRouter PKCE/permanent-key issuer and guarded API-key login publication; native host login remains mandatory

reference.meaning: Existing pinned source read, not a new SDK acquisition or execution. OpenRouter returns a permanent API key, uses S256 and a random callback path without state; no expiring token pair or refresh exchange is inferred.

requirements.implementation: Public beginOpenRouterLogin(callbackUrl, options) returns authorizationUrl/callbackUrl/expiresAt/one-shot complete/cancel. Authorization is fixed openrouter.ai/auth; POST JSON code/code_verifier/code_challenge_method goes only to openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/keys with manual redirects. Hosts supply a loopback HTTP port and generated UUID-v4 callback path; exact origin/path and one bounded code are required on completion, with no invented state requirement. Full callback paste is required, not arbitrary loose-code acceptance. Core owns no listener/browser or environment lookup.
requirements.proof: New useful-flow case checks authorize parameters/no state, independent SHA256 verifier challenge, exact JSON wire/header/no auth and permanent {apiKey} output. Invalid origin/path/duplicate/error/raw-code inputs do not consume the pending flow; valid retry succeeds. Five-minute expiry/unsafe callback rejection, malformed/oversized/denied keys and caller-owned/late hostile-body cancellation refuse without provider-secret reflection.

requirements.requirement: Permanent API-key credentials with the existing encrypted publication fences
requirements.implementation: ProviderCredentialService.prepareApiKeyLogin shares the original one-shot generation/document-revision/CAS/publication/withdrawal machinery with prepareOAuthLogin through a private publisher. The resulting credential is type api-key and not refreshable: no invented lifetime, OAuth refresh token or subscription/account marker. OAuth normalization remains Promise-based; its intended type/version cannot be replaced by input fields. Core bounded OAuth fetch/JSON readers are reused via internal exports, not a new HTTP/store framework.
requirements.proof: Reserved publication precedes exchange, stored key reopens0600 under a foreign storage label and descriptors say api-key/refreshable:false. Concurrent absent-slot logout refuses key publication. Existing OAuth malformed-input normalization still rejects asynchronously and leaves the publisher usable for a subsequent valid candidate. Existing credentials, Radius/Kimi issuer/client and native Server publication controls retain their coverage.

qualification.environment: Docker only; --network none; CI=true; synthetic credentials/disposable stores/mocked transports; no personal credential store, real-account mode or protected-container operation
qualification.build: make typecheck IMAGE_TYPECHECK=ai-harness:mod01-openrouter-oauth-owned; Core/CLI/Server/Web and workspace/parity types PASS

targeted.meaning: Seven new issuer/publication cases plus existing shared credential/device/native-owner controls; no provider/model/host cross-product.

emittedSdk.meaning: Actual public compiled Core root/key exchange/encrypted publication, api-key descriptor and normal Node exit. Mocked service, not installed/production/account/native-host qualification.

counterfactual.meaning: Both selected flows fail on the absent API-key publication entry point before their later PKCE assertions. Do not credit unreached exchange assertions as separate REDs.

retainedFailures.meaning: Initial publisher extraction runs OAuth normalization synchronously, violating the existing Promise rejection contract for a throwing getter. The wrapper is now async; unchanged reproduction passes on the corrected image.

qualification.earlierPasses: focused.log86 and initial emitted.log precede the added normalization reproduction/correction. They are separate source results, not additional final tests or qualification of the corrected wrapper.
qualification.limits: No native OpenRouter CLI/Server/Settings listener/paste/login composition, new inference/account filtering, browser/installed/production/global/real-account or MOD-01.04b proof. Existing API-key A/C/I/T adapters remain unchanged; this SDK alone is not a usable host integration. No SDK acquisition, MOD-03 redelivery, assertion/deadline/flag weakening or historical incident repair/acceptance extension.
